actuation: pneumatic actuation (positive pressure and vacuum) using two side-by-side air chambers per finger
constitutive_assumptions: Quasi-static condition assumed during finger actuation sweeps via slow command trajectories
Fingertip-to-object contact modeled as rolling contact without slipping
Curvature along the finger grasping axis assumed to follow a circular arc, computed using a least-squares circle fit from three marker points
No analytical continuum or hyperelastic constitutive strain-energy formulations were derived or fitted in the text
control_variables: Palm dimensions: flat circular palm of 70 mm diameter positioned 40 mm below fingertip contact points (raised by 10 mm for designated object trials)
Finger geometric specifications: 100 mm bending segment length, 22.5 mm width, 14 short bellows, and 2 mm wall thickness
Finger mounting orientation: two antipodal pairs arranged perpendicularly on a rigid scaffold with a 40-degree angle between opposing fingers in each pair
Mechanical testing displacement: 10 mm crosshead deflection on Instron machine for unactuated stiffness and off-axis grasp stiffness testing
Standard test cylinder diameters: 76.2 mm for pull-out grip strength tests and 25 mm for grasp stiffness vs. angle tests
Experimental trial counts: n = 3 trials for blocked force, stiffness, and grip strength measurements; n = 20 cycles for continuous rotation gait tests
dependent_variables: Fingertip workspace and spatial deflection range (grasping displacement and lateral displacement)
Finger curvature in the grasping axis as a function of actuation pressure
Blocked output force in the grasping direction and lateral direction
Unactuated finger stiffness along the grasping and side-to-side axes
Burst pressure of soft actuator chambers
Hand grip strength / maximum vertical pull force (sustainable object mass)
Grasp stiffness under off-axis angular loading (about major and minor axes)
Planar reachable workspace of manipulated objects (translational area and rotation angle)
Parasitic off-axis motion (extraneous angular rotation during translation, and lateral drift during rotation)
Angular displacement per finger gait cycle
Stability and success of in-hand manipulation tasks and gravity-compensated reorientation

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Dual-chamber pneumatic bellows fingers provide two degrees of freedom per finger, achieving an 80 mm range in the primary grasping axis and ±30 mm of lateral range with roughly linear grasping curvature between 0 and 138 kPa.

The soft finger design exhibits directional stiffness anisotropy, being roughly 4.7 times stiffer in the lateral axis (209.6 ± 13.9 N/m) than in the grasping axis (44.5 ± 3.7 N/m) in an unactuated state.

Adding soft silicone fingertip pads (Eco-flex 00-30, Shore 00-30) increases hand grip strength by more than twentyfold (from 0.21 N to 4.7 N at 173 kPa for a four-finger grasp on a 76.2 mm cylinder) compared to bare/harder fingertips.

A four-finger cross hand configuration executes planar translation across diverse object geometries within a similar circular workspace (~50 mm diameter), whereas rotational range scales inversely with object diameter.

An open-loop heuristic finger gait parameterized solely by nominal pressure (pg) and differential pressure deviation (δ) achieves continuous 360-degree rotation across varied object shapes and sizes over 20 cycles without tactile feedback or trajectory re-planning.

Finger droop caused by object mass under gravity can cause objects to be dropped during reorientation, but can be compensated by superimposing vertical translation pressure offsets onto the rotation gait.

experimental_setup: Actuator fabrication: Injection molding of soft silicone cores (True Skin 10) inside 3D-printed molds (VeroClear), followed by molding of the main finger body using Smooth-Sil 945 silicone (45 Shore-A) and fingertip pads using Ecoflex 00-30 silicone (30 Shore-00); assembly with 3D-printed rigid hubs, Sil-Poxy adhesive, Kevlar thread reinforcement, and heat-shrink tubing

Scaffold and palm assembly: 3D-printed Onyx scaffold and 70 mm flat circular palm mounted with four fingers in two perpendicular antipodal pairs (40-degree angle between opposing fingers) attached to a UR5e robot arm mounting flange
Pressure control system: Custom 8-channel pneumatic pressure controller capable of real-time pressure trajectories with 1.4 kPa accuracy over operating ranges from -34 kPa to 250 kPa

Optical tracking: Vicon motion capture arena used to map 3D fingertip workspaces and measure multi-point finger curvature synchronized via MATLAB; Tracker video analysis software used with an underside camera beneath a transparent acrylic ground plane to calculate planar object poses from fiducial markers

Mechanical loading and force characterization: Instron universal testing machine with a 10 N load cell evaluating blocked force (0–250 kPa), unactuated cantilever stiffness (10 mm displacement in x and y), pull-out grip strength on a 76.2 mm cylinder, and off-axis grasp stiffness on a 25 mm cylinder across 0 to 90 degrees
Robotic manipulation setup: 6-DOF UR5e robot arm executing jar uncapping and mid-air translation, cupcake reorienting and packaging, and gravity-compensated rotation

Test objects: Rigid cylinders (YCB set: 47 mm and 88 mm), rigid cube (60 mm), compliant memory foam block (50 x 50 x 70 mm), food items (muffins of 40 mm and 70 mm, broccoli crown of ~110 mm), plastic jar with screw cap, and cupcakes
future_work: Incorporating a soft palm constructed from compliant components to improve in-hand manipulation performance
Developing mathematical models of soft finger motion to enhance manipulation planning and execution

independent_variables: Actuation pressure and vacuum applied to finger bellows chambers (ranging from -34 kPa to 250 kPa; nominal grasping pressure of 138 kPa; differential pressure deviation δ up to 34 kPa)
Number of active fingers involved in grasp (two fingers vs. four fingers)
Fingertip contact interface material (bare/harder silicone body vs. soft Ecoflex 00-30 compliant finger pads)
Loading orientation angle relative to the hand/cylinder major and minor axes (0 to 90 degrees)
Object physical properties: geometry (cylinders, cubes, irregular produce), size/diameter (40 mm to ~110 mm), and compliance (rigid, memory foam, delicate food items)
Hand orientation relative to the gravity vector (with and without gravity-compensation pressure offsets)
limitations_inferred: The quasi-static operation regime and slow pressure trajectories mean high-speed dynamic in-hand manipulation remains unverified
Maximum payload is restricted to under 0.5 kg (maximum grip strength ~4.7 N), limiting application to lightweight objects
The open-loop finger gait relies on rolling contact without slip; objects with low or uneven friction could experience unmodeled slip or loss of grasp stability
Long-term cyclic fatigue and durability of elastomer chambers, adhesive joints, and thread bindings under repetitive pressure/vacuum cycling were not characterized
Gravity compensation requires prior estimation or knowledge of object mass and hand orientation, lacking autonomous load sensing
limitations_stated_by_authors: Compliance causes significant finger droop under gravitational forces from object weight, which leads to dropped objects during rotation if not compensated
Passive compliance and open-loop control can fail without on-board sensing when loading conditions become unfavorable
System lacks on-board sensors for measuring finger shape or contact forces
No visual perception was integrated into the closed-loop system; object placement and arm poses were predefined
No mathematical models of finger motion were utilized for motion planning
The current palm is rigid rather than soft, which may limit manipulation performance
Smaller objects experience higher undesired angular deflection during translation due to rotational instabilities on high-curvature surfaces
There is an inherent trade-off between grasping force and lateral range of motion when chambers are actuated differentially
main_results: Dual-chamber soft fingers provide ~80 mm grasping range and ±30 mm lateral range, generating maximum blocked forces of 2.3 N along the grasping axis and 1.2 N laterally, with curvature scaling linearly with pressure up to 138 kPa.
Unactuated fingers exhibit 4.7-fold higher lateral stiffness (209.6 N/m) than grasping-axis stiffness (44.5 N/m), providing stability against off-axis disturbances.
Soft silicone fingertip pads increase grip strength from 0.21 N to 4.7 N at 173 kPa (four-finger grasp), enabling secure grasping of payloads up to 0.47 kg.
Grasp stiffness degrades linearly under rotation about the cylinder's major axis and more rapidly under lateral rotation, reaching a minimum of 30–35 N/m at 90 degrees (perpendicular to palm).

Planar translation achieves a uniform ~50 mm diameter circular workspace across all evaluated objects, whereas rotational range is inversely proportional to object diameter; extraneous lateral translation during pure rotation stays within 12 mm.

A two-parameter open-loop heuristic finger gait executes continuous multi-cycle rotation across diverse shapes, sizes, and compliances over 20 consecutive cycles without requiring tactile sensing or re-planning.

Demonstrated practical delicate manipulation in three real-world tasks: jar uncapping with mid-air translation, cupcake reorienting and packaging, and gravity compensation via vertical pressure offsets to prevent dropped objects.
modeling_methods: Least-squares circular fitting applied to three tracked marker coordinates along the finger to measure curvature under varying actuation pressure
Quasi-static kinematic assumption for slow commanded finger motion profiles
Kinematic contact assumption of rolling without slip at the fingertip interface
No analytical or numerical constitutive mechanics models (e.g., beam theory, hyperelastic strain-energy functions, or finite element models) were formulated
performance_metrics: Maximum blocked output force: 2.3 N (grasping axis, dual-chamber actuation), 0.8 N (grasping axis, single-chamber), 1.2 N (lateral axis, single-chamber)
Unactuated finger stiffness: 44.5 ± 3.7 N/m (grasping axis), 209.6 ± 13.9 N/m (side-to-side lateral axis)
Burst pressure: 310 kPa (maximum operating pressure 240 kPa; nominal grasping pressure 138 kPa)
Maximum grip strength: 4.7 N with 4 fingers and soft pads at 173 kPa (holding objects up to 0.47 kg); 0.21 N without soft pads
Off-axis grasp stiffness: 30–35 N/m at 90-degree perpendicular orientation
Planar translation workspace: ~50 mm diameter circular region across test objects
Extraneous lateral drift during rotation: within 12 mm across all objects
Continuous rotation gait displacement: average angular displacement per cycle across 20 cycles per object (ranging from ~10 to 45 deg/cycle depending on diameter)
possible_gap_implications: While passive compliance and open-loop pressure control eliminate sensor complexity for basic manipulation primitives, the absence of closed-loop contact and shape sensing prevents autonomous slip detection and error recovery in unstructured settings.

Relying on hand-tuned heuristic pressure waypoints without predictive continuum or contact mechanics models restricts generalization to arbitrary three-dimensional manipulation trajectories or unknown object dynamics.
The necessity of manual gravity compensation using prior mass knowledge highlights an open gap in autonomous in-hand payload identification and real-time adaptive compliance control.
paper.research_objective: To design, fabricate, and experimentally evaluate a four-fingered soft robotic hand with two-chamber dexterous soft fingers capable of performing planar translation and rotation primitives, as well as continuous in-hand finger gaiting on delicate objects without requiring local sensing or complex closed-loop control.
paper.research_problem: Real-world manipulation requires robots to manage significant uncertainty in object shape, size, and pose, often in confined spaces or with fragile objects; conventional rigid hands require complex models, extensive planning, or heavy computation for in-hand manipulation, while most soft grasping workflows require setting objects onto external surfaces to re-grasp.
stiffness_mechanism: structural compliance from bellows geometry and silicone elastomer
paper.title: A Dexterous Soft Robotic Hand for Delicate In-Hand Manipulation
